Dispersal kernels

geo_dispersal_kernel.Rd

geo_dispersal_kernel() describes the dispersal kernel used by geo_shift_simulate() and geo_epidemic_simulate() on a grid of a given cell size: its realised mean distance (after truncation at max_distance and discretisation on the grid), the share of dispersal beyond five times the mean (the long-distance tail), and the number of neighbouring cells it reaches. Use it to choose between the exponential and the fat-tailed 2Dt kernel and to check that the grid resolves the kernel (cells much smaller than the mean distance).

Usage

geo_dispersal_kernel(
  dispersal_mean,
  cell_size,
  kernel = c("exponential", "2Dt"),
  kernel_shape = 1,
  max_distance = NULL
)

Arguments

dispersal_mean

Mean dispersal distance per step, in metres.

cell_size

Cell size in metres.

kernel

"exponential" or "2Dt" (fat-tailed).

kernel_shape

Shape \(p\) of the 2Dt kernel (above 0.5; smaller is fatter-tailed).

max_distance

Largest dispersal distance in metres (kernel truncation); default five times the mean for the exponential kernel and ten times for the 2Dt kernel.

Value

A one-row tibble: kernel, kernel_shape, dispersal_mean, max_distance, realised_mean, share_beyond_5mean, neighbours.

Examples

geo_dispersal_kernel(500, cell_size = 50)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   kernel      kernel_shape dispersal_mean max_distance realised_mean
#>   <chr>              <dbl>          <dbl>        <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 exponential           NA            500         2500          502.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: share_beyond_5mean <dbl>, neighbours <int>
geo_dispersal_kernel(500, cell_size = 50, kernel = "2Dt", kernel_shape = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   kernel kernel_shape dispersal_mean max_distance realised_mean
#>   <chr>         <dbl>          <dbl>        <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 2Dt               1            500         5000          465.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: share_beyond_5mean <dbl>, neighbours <int>
